Stroud Valley Community School
Looking for a Reception place for September 2027?
Take a look at our Admissions page for exciting new events to showcase our school.
Welcome to Stroud Valley Community Primary School!
I am delighted to be the newly appointed Head Teacher at Stroud Valley Primary School. This is truely a warm, welcoming place and the school motto, "Children at the heart of everything we do," is clearly evident as you walk around the school and see what is on offer.
We are incredibly lucky to have a dedicated team who go above and beyond to support every child, both academically and personally. As a community school, we believe that strong partnerships between home and school help children thrive. We value open communication, so if you ever need anything, please reach out—we’re here to support you and your family.
At Stroud Valley, we work hard to create a safe, nurturing, and engaging environment where young children can flourish. Our curriculum is broad and exciting, and we love to make the most of opportunities like the Stroud Book Festival and our much-loved annual pantomime. Pupils are happy here, they engage in their learning well and are lucky to have such an enriched offer of activities available.
If you would like to visit our school prior to admissions, please call the school office on 01453 764400 and we can arrange a suitable time for a show around.
If you require a paper copy of any of the information on this website please contact Morag Cartwright or Anna Dutton in the main office.

pageCache.pageTitle: Stroud Valley Community School: Breakfast Club and After School Care
pageCache.text:
Breakfast Club and After School Care
Breakfast Club starts at 8.00am, the cost is £4.00. If you wish to bring your child at 7.45am the cost is £4.50. Your child will receive a healthy breakfast and have a play before school starts.
After School Care runs from 3.15pm - 5.30pm. Pricing structures are as follows:
Option 1: 3.15pm - 4.30pm -£6
Option 2: 3.15pm - 5.00pm- £8.40
Option 3: 4.15pm - 5.00pm- £3.60
Option 4: 4.15pm-5.30pm - £6
Option 5: 3.15pm-5.30pm £10.80
Please make sure you book in advance. There will be a late charge of £20 if you collect your child after 5.30pm.
All breakfast and after school care sessions must be booked using our online bookable sysem on ParentPay (www.parentpay.com). This is to ensure the ratio of staff to children is correct as safeguarding of our pupils is paraount. It will be the parental responsibility to book and pay for all sessions via ParentPay in advance.
Sessions need to be paid for at the time of booking or sessions will be cancelled by the system and your child's place may be lost.
Sessions need to be booked, amended or canceled before midday of the previous day. Any last-minute bookings or changes must be made through the school office. Any sessions not cancelled will still be charged.
If you are in receipt of voucher payments or tax-free child care, we will credit your account accordingly once you have notified us.

pageCache.text:
PSHE & RSE
PSHE and Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) are invaluable parts of every child's education and at Stroud Valley we want to help shape learners who are confident, respectful and responsible members of society. We create a safe, inclusive and supportive environment where children feel valued and encouraged to share their ideas, ask questions and develop a positive understanding of themselves and others. We make meaningful links with everyday life so that children can see how the knowledge and skills they learn will help them now and in the future, showing them that everyone can make positive choices and reach their full potential.
We want children to develop the knowledge, skills and confidence to build healthy relationships, understand and manage their emotions, keep themselves physically and mentally healthy, and make informed and responsible decisions. Through discussion, reflection and collaborative learning, children learn to respect different views, celebrate diversity and understand the importance of kindness, empathy and resilience. We encourage children to recognise that making mistakes is part of learning and to develop the confidence to solve problems, seek support when needed and make positive choices.
Our aim is to nurture caring, resilient and independent learners who are well prepared for life beyond primary school. By promoting respect, inclusion, wellbeing and personal responsibility, we equip children with the understanding and confidence to stay safe, contribute positively to their communities and become happy, healthy and responsible citizens.

Governors
The Governing Body consist of two committees: Finance, Staffing and Premises and Self Evaluation. The full Governing Body also meet once a term and chairs of each committee feed back information about their committee work. If you would like to speak to a member of the Governing Body please ring the school office to make an appointment or ask a Governor to contact you. If you would like a copy of the minutes from the latest Full Governing Body meeting, please ask the Chair using the email below:
GOVERNOR UPDATES
The Governing Body met at the end of last term and elected a new Chair and Vice-Chair. Christine Minett was elected as Chair - she has been a governor at the school for over 25 years and her lifelong career has been in supporting employment and further education. James Vandenbergh-Harwood was elected as Vice-Chair. James has been a parent governor for 3 years and has over 18 years experience working within finance and strategy.
Christine Minett (Chair of Governors, Finance, Staffing and Premises Committee - Chair)
I live locally and have been a governor at Stroud Valley Community school for over 25 years. During that time my three children have attended and flourished at the school. I am Chair of the Finance and Staffing Committee and I serve on the Self Evaluation Committee. My lifelong career has been in supporting employment and further education.
Claire Jones (Headteacher)
I am thrilled to have recently joined Stroud Valley as Headteacher and feel privileged to be part of such a wonderful school community. Throughout my career I have been committed to helping every child develop confidence, curiosity, and a love of learning; I know this will continue here in my new role.
When I'm not in school, I enjoy reading, cooking and spending time with my family. I love being away on holiday and my favourite place is always by the sea.
Sarah Heague (Teaching, Learning and Assessment)
As Deputy Head Teacher at Stroud Valley no two days are ever the same. I enjoy teaching as much as I ever did; there’s always something new and exciting taking place! As a teacher governor I support the governing body in interpreting and understanding the curriculum, ensuring we’re all up to date with new initiatives.
Simon Pizzey (Teaching, Learning and Assessment)
I was approached to become a school governor a number of years as a co-opted governor. At the time I was a staff press photographer for local press with many contacts in the local community and in education at all levels. The school was always willing to co-operate with the press at short notice and I developed a good relationship with Debbie Sleep the head teacher. In the year of Brunel’s Bicentenary I ran a workshop based on the famous photograph of Brunel in front of the chains of The Great Eastern Steam Ship and later on pinhole camera workshops. Many of my family members are teachers and I have always been passionate about the value and importance of education particularly at primary level. I have run many photography based workshops from Primary to University. I hold Further and Adult Education Teaching Certificates. In 2014 I was made redundant and re-trained to become a teaching assistant working one day a week in year 6 for a year at Stroud Valley as part of my qualifications through Stroud College. Presently, I work as a freelance photographer and an agency Teaching Assistant mainly supporting Special Needs students in a variety of primary level settings. I have a strong interest in SEN and have personal experience of dyslexia in my family.
James Vandenbergh-Harwood (Parent Governor)
I am James Vandenbergh-Harwood and am a parent governor. I have three girls at the school and wanted to join the governing body to help make a positive difference and ultimately support the school. I have been in banking for around 18 years and currently hold a role in strategy following a number of years in customer facing functions. I will use these skills to support the finance committee and also provide oversight and challenge on a number of areas including the school development plan and vision. In addition to this I am passionate about financial literacy and believe there is a clear link between financial education that we receive as children and our relationship with our finances as adults. I have seen the impact of this first hand from my time as a Director for the Stroud Valley Credit Union. My aim is to support the school to boost this understanding and knowledge over my term as governor.
Alice Moore (Parent Governor)
I joined as a parent governor in 2025 and have a daughter at the school. I grew up locally and attended Stroud Valley myself over 30 years ago. I have worked in the voluntary sector for almost two decades, with a focus on social inclusion and equity. I sit on the Self Evaluation Committee with a particular link to humanities.
Lisa Hinkley (Co-opted Governor)
I am a retired local primary head teacher who worked for many years with other local head teachers in the Stroud Association of Schools. I have lived in Stroud for 26 years with my husband (also a retired Head Teacher). We enjoyed bringing our three daughters up in this lovely town.
Having retired I would like to use my knowledge and skills to continue to support the education of local children. The school motto, “Children at the heart of everything we do," holds real value for me and I hope that as a governor I can support Stroud Valley in achieving this and giving them the best education.
Claire Murphy (Associate Member)
I studied for my BEd (Primary) in Aberdeen straight from school and graduated in 1992 when at the time education was still in early stages of implementing a National Curriculum and, disillusioned with what that looked like (emphasis on ticking boxes and paperwork rather than children) decided to follow a slightly different career path. Over the next 10 years I was a Trainer (customer service and management development) leading on to being a Training Manager, HR Project Leader, Change Manager and HR Consultant within the contexts of retail, law and various financial services. Whilst I enjoyed these roles, I decided that I didn't want to work for 'The Shareholder' anymore and decided to do a course to return to teaching. Since my return I have worked as a teacher in early years, primary and SEND (Special Educational Needs and Disabilities) settings and led curriculum within SEND.
As a former lead for a Teaching School Alliance and as part of my current role over the last 6 years I have had the pleasure of managing cohorts of trainee teachers through School Direct ITT programmes and co-ordinating/ delivering SEND CPD to mainstream and SEND schools within Gloucestershire and across the South West. As SAND Training & Outreach Manager I am a member of the SAND Academies Trust strategic management team with responsibility for CPD for more than 600 staff as well as our external training and outreach arm. SAND Training & Outreach is a partner of both Odyssey Teaching School Hub and Balcarras Teaching School Hub. As well as being a member of the Strategic Boards for each, I sit on the workstreams to support development and implementation of Initial Teacher Training (ITT), Early Careers Framework (ECF) and Continuous Professional Development (CPD) across Gloucestershire and on behalf of the hubs am Cluster Lead for two clusters of mainstream primary and SEND ECTs in Gloucestershire.
Outside of work I am lucky enough to be mum of Alfie who is 15, and my partner George is lucky enough to have me! I really enjoy SUPping, marathon kayaking (my car is easy to spot with a strange metal contraption on top to carry boats) and getting muddy in the garden...I'm not particularly good at any of them but I am a firm believer in the process rather than the end result!
Julie Howe (Associate Member)
I am an associate member serving on the Finance, Staffing and Premises Committee. Until summer 2021 I had previously served on the full GB since 2015. At the point of stepping down I was asked to continue using my experience to support the finance committee of the school and agree to become an associate member. All three of my children went to SVCS in their primary years. I work in the creative industry.

Music
At Stroud Valley, we believe that music is a powerful form of expression that enriches children's lives and brings people together. We aim to inspire a love of music by providing exciting and inclusive opportunities for every child to perform, listen, compose and appreciate music from a wide range of cultures, traditions and historical periods.
Through practical and engaging experiences, children develop their musical knowledge, skills and confidence. They learn to sing with expression, play tuned and untuned instruments, compose their own music and listen critically to a variety of musical styles. Working both independently and collaboratively, children are encouraged to be creative, resilient and reflective as they explore and develop their musical ideas.
We make meaningful links between music and the wider curriculum, helping children to understand the important role music plays in everyday life, communities and cultures around the world. By experiencing high-quality musical opportunities and learning about influential composers and musicians, children develop an appreciation of music's ability to communicate, inspire and connect people.
Our aim is to nurture confident, creative and enthusiastic musicians who enjoy making music, value the contributions of others and leave Stroud Valley with a lifelong appreciation of music and the confidence to continue their musical journey.

Parents
At our school, we know that parents are their child's first and most important teachers. We want to work closely with you throughout your child's journey, celebrating achievements, communicating openly and supporting one another. Together, we can provide the best possible experience for every child.
We believe that effective communication is at the heart of a successful partnership. We aim to keep parents informed, involved an engaged in school life, welcoming your ideas, questions and feedback as we work together to support your child's learning and wellbeing. We hope you will find the information needed on the website however if you do have any questions please direct these to the school office: [email protected] or [email protected] and refer to our communication flowchart.
We welcome parents as partners in their child's education.
We believe that every child's success is built on a strong partnership between home and school.
Together, we can help every child reach their full potential.
Open communication, mutual respect and shared aspirations are at the heart of everything we do.
We are committed to working alongside parents to ensure every child feels supported, challenged and valued.

Science
Science is a subject that inspires curiosity and helps children make sense of the world around them. At Stroud Valley, we want to develop learners who are excited by science, ask thoughtful questions and have a genuine respect for the natural and physical world. Through a range of practical, hands-on and enquiry-based experiences, we encourage children to explore, investigate and discover, helping them to understand that science is relevant, exciting and an important part of everyday life.
We want children to develop secure scientific knowledge alongside the skills needed to work scientifically. We encourage them to observe carefully, make predictions, plan and carry out investigations, identify patterns, classify, research and draw conclusions using appropriate scientific vocabulary. We know that making mistakes is a valuable part of learning, and we encourage children to think independently, reflect on their findings and learn from their investigations.
We aim to nurture confident, inquisitive learners who enjoy asking questions and solving problems through scientific enquiry. By making meaningful links to previous learning, introducing inspiring scientists and exploring the role of science in today's world, including important global issues such as climate change and future science-related careers, we help children to develop a lifelong interest in science and an understanding of the vital role it plays in shaping our lives and our future.

Curriculum
Statement
Our curriculum is delivered through a rich menu of exciting and motivating learning opportunities, focussed on making creative and flexible links.
Open ended engaging experiences are planned for our children, embracing expertise and enthusiasm from our families, community and beyond to enable children to learn in a purposeful and enriching way.
We teach our children the ‘skills’ of learning; enabling them to understand how successful learners learn. We promote problem solving creativity and communication which enables children to reflect on and evaluate their learning.
We embrace the value of outside learning and maximise our opportunities wherever we can to excite promote and sustain children’s interest e.g. forest school, welcome parents and carers to contribute to specialist learning and developing partnerships with external partners and providers.
Our broad and balanced curriculum encourages and inspires a deeper understanding of the world around us. It also develops self - esteem and confidence in our abilities to reflect and think mindfully about learning and how successful learners learn and take responsibility to shape their future lives as valued citizens.
Through keeping children at the heart of everything we do, we strive to offer diverse and creative opportunities to unlock the potential of each and every child.
Rolling Programme
EYFS
Reception Year Curriculum - Early Years Foundation Stage
The Reception year is where children start their learning journey at Stroud Valley Community Primary School. Some will know each other from nursery, play groups or local childminders, others will find it all new, exciting and maybe a little scary, but by the end of the first term they will all have made lots of new friends and become used to our school’s routines and expectations.
Four guiding principles shape what we do. These are:
• every child is a unique child, who is constantly learning and can be resilient, capable, confident and self-assured
• children learn to be strong and independent through positive relationships
• children learn and develop well in enabling environments, in which their experiences respond to their individual needs and there is a strong partnership between practitioners and parents and/or carers
• children develop and learn in different ways and at different rates.

Miss Nesbitt
The Reception class is where children start their learning journey at Stroud Valley Community School. Some will know each other from nursery, others will find it all new, exciting and maybe a little scary, but by the end of the first term, they will all have made lots of new friends and become used to the school routine. The curriculum supports your child in seven key areas of their development: - Personal, Social & Emotional Development - Communication and Language - Knowledge and Understanding of the World - Mathematics - Physical Development - Literacy - Expressive Arts. In reception we learn through play and by the end of the first year children will be able to read and write a range of words using their phonic knowledge and will to be able to carry out a variety of maths activities. We have an excellent environment which allows the children to 'free flow' between both Sunshine and Rainbow Reception classrooms as well as the outdoors. Miss Nesbitt is your class teacher and Mrs RT is the class TA.
We look forward to working with you all.

Art and Design
Art and Design Intent
Art and Design is a subject that inspires creativity, imagination and self-expression, and at Stroud Valley we want to help shape learners who have a positive attitude towards art and design and a curiosity about the creative world around them. We work in a range of different ways, both individually and collaboratively, encouraging children to experiment, explore and communicate their ideas with confidence. We make links with the real world wherever possible, enabling our children to understand why they are learning these skills and how creativity enriches their lives, showing children that art is enjoyable, meaningful and that everyone CAN be an artist.
We want children to develop their knowledge, skills and understanding through drawing, painting, sculpture and other creative disciplines whilst exploring a wide range of materials, techniques and processes. We encourage children to take risks, experiment and learn from mistakes, developing resilience and confidence as they create, evaluate and refine their own work. By studying the work of a diverse range of artists, craftspeople and designers from different cultures and periods of history, children develop an appreciation of the rich artistic heritage that has shaped our world.
We aim to nurture imaginative, reflective and confident learners who are able to express their ideas, thoughts and emotions creatively. Through meaningful opportunities to observe, create and evaluate, children develop their artistic skills, critical thinking and appreciation of art and design, preparing them to become creative individuals who value the importance of the arts in their own lives and in the wider world.

Computing
Computing is a subject that is invaluable for life and at Stroud Valley we want to help shape learners who have a positive attitude towards computing and an interest in technology and digital innovation. We work in a range of different ways, both individually and collaboratively, developing creativity, problem-solving and computational thinking skills. We make links with the real world wherever possible to enable our children to understand why they are learning these skills and how they will support them in their future lives, showing children that computing is exciting, relevant and that everyone CAN succeed in computing.
We want children to develop confidence in using technology safely, responsibly and effectively, whilst building their understanding of computer science, information technology and digital literacy. Through practical, engaging and hands-on experiences, children learn to create, explore, programme, debug and communicate using a range of digital tools. We encourage children to persevere, learn from mistakes and develop resilience as they solve problems and create digital solutions.
We aim to nurture independent, responsible and curious learners who are prepared for an increasingly digital world. By making meaningful links across the curriculum and helping children understand the importance of online safety and the impact of technology on everyday life, we inspire them to become confident, responsible and capable digital citizens.
Purple Mash
At Stroud Valley we use Purple Mash, award-winning teaching and learning software aimed at KS1 and KS2 children. It helps to develop digital and computing skills, including coding, email, and online safety. The activities and games featured are high quality and are closely linked to many other curriculum areas.

English
English at Stroud Valley Primary School
Learning to speak, listen, read, spell and write are the foundations of our curriculum and are modelled and taught systematically and incidentally (making purposeful links to support the long term memory) throughout the school day.
At Stroud Valley, children are at the heart of everything we do and we want to broaden their experiences not only first-hand but through well written literature. Each class, or year group team, have a pool of whole class texts that aim to enrich the children’s lives. They take them on journeys across seas, oceans, high up mountains and into fantasy worlds where their imaginations can be free and wild.
At Stroud Valley we aim to create writers, who draw on experiences and skills to communicate thoughts, feelings and ideas in a range of contexts and purposes and for a range of audiences, whilst using accurate spelling, grammar and clear handwriting.
Children will then apply these skills as well as the imagination gained from reading, to plan, compose and edit, which will in turn, allow children to work collaboratively with their peers as well as taking responsibility for their own learning.
Through the use of high- quality texts as a foundation and stimulus from which to build from, we aim to develop children into confident, creative writers. We passionately believe that developing secure and accomplished writers raises attainment across the curriculum and beyond. By the end of their journey, our intent is that our children have acquired a solid understanding of grammar, built a bank of rich vocabulary and have the confidence to experiment with language, depending on audience and purpose. We encourage our children to be reflective, take pride in their presentation and to perfect their planning and editing skills. Carefully selected relevant, engaging literature inspires our children to produce purposeful writing outcomes that develop both composition and transcription.
Alongside composition, children will be taught: spelling, punctuation, grammar and handwriting skills both discreetly and within units of work.
At Stroud Valley Primary School, we strive to provide an ambitious curriculum that generates a genuine love for writing and the written word in our children, encouraging them to see writing as an interesting and enjoyable process. It is our intention that children learn to speak, read and write fluently.
We aim to foster a love of language and literature through the use of quality texts and books; that inspires, excites and engages our children and encourages them to be able to communicate through speaking, listening and writing. This is supported by a clear skills and knowledge progression. We aim to develop children’s ability to produce well-structured, detailed writing in which the meaning is made clear and which engages the interest of the reader. Particular attention is paid throughout the school to the formal structures of English: grammatical detail and punctuation.
We recognise the need to focus on vocabulary in order to develop writing – if a child can’t say it then they can’t write it. In order for children to reach their full potential we know they must develop strength and stamina for extended writing; being able to use fluent and legible handwriting.

Geography
At Stroud Valley, we believe that geography helps children to understand the world they live in and their place within it. We aim to inspire curiosity and fascination about the Earth's people, places and environments, equipping children with the knowledge and skills to make sense of an ever-changing world.
Through engaging, enquiry-based learning, children explore a wide range of physical and human geography, from their local area to the wider world. They develop their understanding of how places are connected, how environments are shaped and how people interact with the world around them. Through fieldwork, map work, digital technologies and the use of a range of geographical sources, children learn to observe, question, investigate and communicate their findings with increasing confidence.
We encourage children to think critically about important global issues, including sustainability, climate change and the responsible use of natural resources. By making meaningful links between geography and everyday life, we help children to appreciate cultural diversity, respect different communities and understand the importance of caring for our planet.
Our aim is to develop confident, knowledgeable and responsible geographers who are curious about the world, value its diversity and are prepared to contribute positively as informed global citizens throughout their lives.
